title: Jaypal Malviya Wins World Silver, Secures India's First LA 2028 Quota
excerpt: The little-known pistol shooter scored 242.2 in the Doha final behind China's Hu Kai, and India's women took team silver the same morning.
body:
• Jaypal Malviya won silver in the men's 10m air pistol at the ISSF World Championships in Doha on November 5, scoring 242.2 in the 24-shot final.
  • China's Hu Kai took gold with 243.9 and Czechia's Jindrich Dubovy bronze with 220.9; all three medalists earned Los Angeles 2028 quota places.
  • Malviya's is India's first quota place for LA 2028. A quota belongs to the country, not the shooter — India's team will be decided at selection trials in 2028.
  • India's women's 10m air pistol team — Manu Bhaker, Suruchi Inder Singh and Sainyam — won team silver the same morning with an aggregate of 1738.

A shooter most Indian fans had not heard of a week ago has opened India's account for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. Jaypal Malviya won the silver medal in the men's 10m air pistol at the ISSF World Championship in Doha on Thursday, November 5, and with it secured India's first quota place for LA 2028, according to IANS reporting from the Lusail Shooting Complex. RevSportz described him as the man no one knew, arriving like a storm on the biggest stage.

How the final was won and lost

Three Olympic quota spots were on offer in the event. Malviya shot 242.2 in the 24-shot final to finish second, behind China's Hu Kai, who took gold and the first quota with 243.9. Czechia's Jindrich Dubovy won bronze and the third quota with 220.9. Malviya was in medal contention from the opening stage — 50.5 in the first series and 100.0 at the end of the second — and in the elimination stages fired consistent high-10s, including hits of 10.8 and 10.7, to separate himself from the chasing pack and hold Dubovy at bay in the final shots. He had qualified third with 585-23x, a series of 97, 99, 97, 99, 97, 96 that also led India's seventh-place men's team effort of 1730-58x. Kamaljeet shot 580-20x to finish 27th in qualifying and Ravin Kumar recorded 565-15x.

"Kamaljeet shot 580-20x to finish 27th in qualifying and Ravin Kumar recorded 565-15x."

A second silver the same morning

Earlier in the morning session, the Indian women's 10m air pistol squad clinched the team silver medal. Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker, Suruchi Inder Singh and Sainyam combined for an aggregate of 1738 with 61 inner 10s. Manu led the Indian challenge with 583-21x, including a perfect 100 in her fourth series; Suruchi contributed 580-24x and junior world champion Sainyam added 575-16x. China took the women's team gold with 1745-65x and the Republic of Korea claimed bronze with 1729-49x.

What the quota does and does not guarantee

The quota place belongs to India, not to Malviya personally, as SportsBackstory's report notes: the Indian team for Los Angeles will be decided after the Olympic selection trials in 2028, and the Doha championships are the first qualification event for those Games. Malviya has therefore won his country a place and himself a head start in the argument — nothing more, and nothing less. For a shooter who arrived in Doha as an unfamiliar name, that is a substantial day's work.
image_caption: Jaypal Malviya, left, holds his silver medal on the podium at the ISSF World Championships in Doha, with gold medalist Hu Kai of China, centre, and bronze medalist Jindrich Dubovy of Czechia. Malviya's second place secured India's first quota place for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.
